articles.title: Home Assistant gives people, devices and zones their own map views
articles.dek: A redesigned panel organizes household location history into three tabs, with clearer markers and information bubbles.
body: Home Assistant separates people, devices and zones into their own tabs on its map, giving households distinct views of the locations they follow. The redesigned panel currently focuses on location history.

Maarten Lakerveld pairs the panel with new map markers and information bubbles. The marker design works across both of Home Assistant’s map engines, keeping the same treatment as the underlying map changes. Bram Kragten reviewed the implementation.

media.alt: Home Assistant map of Amsterdam with redesigned Home and Train zone markers and a list of zones.
media.caption: The redesigned zone markers on Home Assistant’s map.

articles.title: ELTAKO donates CHF 25,000 to the Open Home Foundation
articles.dek: The Works with Home Assistant partner adds a donation to its support for the foundation.
body: ELTAKO has donated 25,000 Swiss francs to the Open Home Foundation, according to Paulus Schoutsen’s September newsletter. The maker of relay switches, sensors and building controls is already a Works with Home Assistant partner and has taken part in community meetups, State of the Open Home and the foundation’s IFA visit.

externalSources.title: Thirteen years of Home Assistant: Leading the way back home

articles.title: Home Assistant confines Telegram downloads to approved folders
articles.dek: Automations using a custom download destination need that folder in Home Assistant’s allowlist; the default location stays unchanged.
body: Home Assistant’s Telegram download action stops accepting an arbitrary destination folder. A custom directory must be inside the configured allowlist, preventing the action from creating files elsewhere on the server, including through a symbolic link that leaves the allowed directory.

Franck Nijhof’s correction changes what existing automations may need: a custom destination must be added to allowlist_external_dirs. Downloads that omit the destination continue to use the telegram_bot folder inside Home Assistant’s configuration directory without an additional setting.

pullRequests.title: Contain the download directory in telegram_bot.download_file

articles.title: Home Assistant controls LinkPlay music from any speaker in the group
articles.dek: Follower speakers show the playing track and pass playback commands to their group leader while retaining their own volume.
body: A LinkPlay speaker playing in a group can leave its Home Assistant control showing an unknown track and buttons that do nothing. The integration takes the track information from the group’s lead speaker and sends playback commands there, so the controls for any member operate the music it is playing.

Mickael Goubin makes track title, artist, album, artwork and playback progress follow the leader. Each speaker keeps its own volume, mute, source selection and sound mode, and its follower role remains visible.

pullRequests.title: Make LinkPlay followers mirror and control the group leader

articles.title: ESPHome repairs encrypted updates in recovery mode
articles.dek: Devices using their configured connection key can accept a repair upload even when normal startup fails.
body: ESPHome repairs encrypted firmware uploads for devices that cannot start normally and have entered safe mode. When the update key comes from the device’s configured Home Assistant connection key, a repair upload could fail on RP2040 devices or crash other chips.

J. Nick Koston makes the configured key available without starting the normal device connection. Keys supplied later through that connection can also be recovered from saved settings, although a storage limitation on ESP8266 and RP2040 can still prevent those devices from offering encryption in safe mode.

pullRequests.title: [esphome] Keep the OTA encryption key without the api server so safe mode uploads work

articles.title: Music Assistant wakes sleeping Sonos speakers for playback
articles.dek: Move and Roam speakers can wake over the network instead of needing someone to press their power button.
body: Music Assistant wakes compatible Sonos portable speakers when someone starts playback or turns the player on. Battery-powered Move, Move 2 and Roam speakers previously appeared unavailable after going to sleep, leaving people to wake them physically.

Marvin Schenkel adds the network wake request for speakers that advertise support for it, with a real Move 2 responding in about three seconds. The feature uses the player’s native power control. Turning it off in Music Assistant does not put the speaker to sleep remotely; Sonos still handles that through its own idle timer.

pullRequests.title: Wake sleeping Sonos portable speakers automatically

articles.title: Assist fills the gaps in translated error messages
articles.dek: Missing responses across 64 language sets stop falling back to generic English, using a first pass of machine-generated translations.
body: Assist gains translated responses for errors that previously fell back to generic English. Sixty-four of its 65 language sets were missing at least one of the 31 error messages; 26 languages had only the six original responses.

Michael Hansen fills those gaps and fixes existing responses that used the wrong device or location information. Two Russian templates that could fail instead of producing a reply are repaired too. The new translations are explicitly a machine-generated first pass, with native speakers invited to improve the wording.

pullRequests.title: Complete error messages for all languages

articles.title: Gree air conditioners gain infrared control in Home Assistant
articles.dek: A new integration builds on the shared infrared protocol found in Gree, Onida and Sinclair equipment.
body: Gree air conditioners gain an infrared integration in Home Assistant, adding another route for equipment operated by an infrared remote. Dr.Blank connects the integration to the shared infrared-protocol library.

The work began with captures from an Onida remote. Comparison with a Sinclair unit and tests using Gree signal timings established that the protocol belongs to Gree, leading to the broader name. The evidence supports compatible equipment using that protocol, rather than every model sold under those brands.

pullRequests.title: Add documentation for Gree Infrared integration
Add Onida AC IR protocol encoder and decoder
Rename the Onida AC protocol to Gree

articles.title: Music Assistant picks up new Plex albums without the scheduled wait
articles.dek: An optional setting starts synchronization when Plex reports a changed library, keeping the regular schedule as a fallback.
body: Music Assistant gains an option to synchronize a Plex music library when Plex finishes scanning new content. That avoids waiting for the next scheduled synchronization, which runs every 12 hours by default. RyanAtTanagra saw a newly added album appear about 20 seconds later in a test with a real Plex server.

The “Sync when the Plex library changes” setting checks that the library’s contents actually changed before starting work. It reconnects if the notification connection drops, while the regular synchronization schedule remains in place.

pullRequests.title: Sync a Plex library as soon as Plex reports that it changed

articles.title: Kiosk Satellite puts voice and music on Android control panels
articles.dek: The community project listens for a wake word with the screen off and plays music through Sendspin.
body: An Android tablet serving as a Home Assistant control panel can also listen for a wake word while its screen is off, according to the Open Home Foundation’s September newsletter. It highlights Xavier Larrea’s Kiosk Satellite, which combines the panel with Sendspin music playback and photo screensavers. The newsletter also describes triggering actions by holding up fingers to the tablet’s camera.

articles.title: Adding a HEOS speaker keeps the rest of the group
articles.dek: Home Assistant preserves existing group members when another room joins.
body: Adding a third HEOS speaker to a group in Home Assistant could remove the second one. The integration preserves the current members when adding a player, instead of replacing the group with only the speakers named in the latest command.

Chris reproduced the problem with three devices and makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the correction. Removing a speaker uses the unjoin action; joining a speaker to itself no longer dissolves its existing group.

pullRequests.title: Keep existing HEOS group members when joining a player

articles.title: Voice Preview Edition prepares encrypted storage and signed updates
articles.dek: A new factory firmware path protects saved settings and checks update signatures; existing units need a separate migration.
body: Nabu Casa prepares a factory firmware path for Home Assistant Voice Preview Edition that encrypts saved settings, verifies firmware signatures and blocks update downgrades. Keith Burzinski connects it to Nabu Casa’s signing and distribution system, with a 15-minute timeout for initial provisioning.

Existing units keep their current ESPHome update channel and need a separate migration. Developers who manually flash this configuration over USB onto an existing unit permanently program an encryption key into the chip and clear its saved preferences once, including Wi-Fi credentials and the Home Assistant connection key.

pullRequests.title: Add EN 18031 compliance: NVS encryption, signed OTA, provisioning timeout

roadmapUpdates.title: Receiving radio commands gains roadmap approval
roadmapUpdates.summary: Home Assistant’s plan to receive radio-frequency commands moves from Awaiting approval to Approved after Abílio Costa offers to work through the remaining design. The approval advances the opportunity without establishing a release date.

roadmapUpdates.title: The Modbus panel also covers legacy connections
roadmapUpdates.summary: Paulus Schoutsen confirms that frontend work for the Modbus connection panel is complete and includes legacy connections. The opportunity remains in Building, with no release identified in his update.

roadmapUpdates.title: Green Power work gains a medium priority
roadmapUpdates.summary: The plan to pair and manage battery-free Zigbee devices in ZHA gains a Medium priority. Matthias Kerstner confirms the team’s agreement on its move to Building, reported yesterday; no delivery date is set.
